answer: A bond of 29% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in basalt, and island reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 42 aliases, and each one needs its own funded bridge account. That bill is paid per identity, so 240 aliases cost 250 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
